## Data availability

This analysis focuses on low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) with estimates or household survey data that collect information on equity, as well as selected analysis on equity in upper-middle- and high-income countries with vital registration data.

Most of the data used in this analysis are from nationally representative household surveys. For under-five mortality rates by wealth quintile and under-five and neonatal mortality rates by subnational area, UN IGME<sup>69, 70</sup> produces annual trend estimates that are used. The estimates are informed by household survey data, and a statistical model is fitted to the data to generate trend estimates and averages over the results from household surveys. All other disaggregated mortality estimates – for all dimensions analyzed – are based on nationally representative household survey data or sample vital registration data. In addition, we compiled subnational mortality data from vital registration systems in upper-middle- and high-income countries – mainly in Europe, Northern America, Australia and New Zealand – as well as mortality data by ethnicity in Australia and Brazil.

Data were not available for all countries. Wealth quintile under-five estimates were available for `r code_number_display(calc_black(wealth_country_count, digits = 0, evidence = "IGME2025_U5MR_wealth_quintile_projection_country.csv"), "code-number-0425")` countries from empirical survey or sample vital registration data, while `r code_number_display(calc_black(birth_interval_selected[['countries']], digits = 0, evidence = "country-specific-database-cleaned-igme-wealth_2026-06-23.csv"), "code-number-0426")` countries (or less) were included in the analysis of wealth quintile neonatal mortality, education, residence, mother’s age, birth interval, birth order and birth size (see Table 1). For different disaggregations, the number of countries vary a bit because not every category in the equity dimension had sufficient cases for comparison across categories.

Mortality rates for the different disaggregations were mostly calculated from microdata (`r code_number_display(calc_black(microdata_surveys, digits = 0, evidence = "country-specific empirical database"), "code-number-0427")` surveys for `r code_number_display(calc_black(microdata_countries, digits = 0, evidence = "country-specific empirical database"), "code-number-0428")` countries); or, in the absence of microdata, obtained from reports or websites (`r code_number_display(calc_black(nonmicro_surveys, digits = 0, evidence = "country-specific empirical database"), "code-number-0429")` surveys or sample vital registration systems for `r code_number_display(calc_black(nonmicro_countries, digits = 0, evidence = "country-specific empirical database"), "code-number-0430")` countries). In total, almost `r code_number_display(calc_black(round(empirical_rows, digits = -3), digits = 0, evidence = "country-specific empirical database"), "code-number-0431")` data points from empirical data sources were included in this analysis. Among household survey and sample vital registration data, we selected the most recent quality data point by disaggregation.

Table 1 below provides an overview of the selection criteria applied to country data by equity dimension, ranging from socio-economic factors to demographic variables. We selected the most recent source since 2013 in a country, excluding data sources with low quality and estimates for small countries with less than `r calc_black(selection_rules$minimum_live_births, digits = 0, evidence = "analysis selection rule")` live births in 2024. For countries with more than one quality survey since 2013, we selected the most recent. While all the UN IGME estimates are available up to the year 2024, survey estimates refer to a 5-year or 10-year period before the survey. If possible, the 5-year period was used but in some cases 10-year intervals were used. For the few cases of sample vital registration (Bangladesh, China and India) the most recent available annual data were used.

## Calculation of aggregates and adjustments

Aggregated mortality rates were calculated to summarize the disparities across the equity dimensions for the selected countries in this analysis. For comparability, the rates from empirical data were adjusted to the UN IGME national estimates for the year 2024. As a next step the number of deaths in each equity group were calculated using the respective number of births with the distribution of births by equity group in the surveys applied to the live births from World Population Prospects 2024 Revision<sup>71</sup> for the year 2024. After the deaths and births in each group were summed up, the aggregated mortality rate was calculated for each group.

For the neonatal mortality rate (NMR) by wealth quintile in the country analysis and for the aggregates, the rates were adjusted to the UN IGME estimate of under-five mortality rate (U5MR) by wealth quintile using the following steps: First, the ratio of NMR to U5MR was calculated from the most recent survey data in each wealth quintile in a country. Second, this ratio was multiplied by the UN IGME U5MR estimates by wealth quintile in the country in the year 2024 to obtain the adjusted NMR for each quintile in the country. The adjusted NMR was used as input for the calculation of the aggregate for countries with available quality data. For Kosovo<sup>*</sup>, no UN IGME estimates by wealth quintile were available to adjust to. The same approach was used for the 1–59-months mortality rate.

## Trend analysis

To analyse time trends by equity, the most recent data point from each available survey was selected with at least three data points over time to enable trend estimation. This meant about `r note_number(floor(min(trend_retention_percent) / 10) * 10, "70", "country-p75-retention-low", "country_projection_2000_2024_from_extrapolation_benchmarked.xlsx; country retention; outward rounding to tens")`–`r note_number(ceiling(max(trend_retention_percent) / 10) * 10, "80", "country-p75-retention-high", "country_projection_2000_2024_from_extrapolation_benchmarked.xlsx; country retention; outward rounding to tens")` per cent of the countries per equity dimension were kept in the analysis, ranging from `r code_number_display(calc_black(trend_min_country_count, digits = 0, evidence = "trend_summary_nc_2000_2024_PD.csv"), "code-number-0433")` countries (for mother’s age) to `r code_number_display(calc_black(trend_max_country_count, digits = 0, evidence = "trend_summary_nc_2000_2024_PD.csv"), "code-number-0434")` countries (for residence). In the next step, linear models were fit separately for each country and each equity dimension using the log-transformed mortality estimates, and these models were used to extrapolate values from 2000 to 2024. For comparability, the rates were adjusted from empirical data to the UN IGME national estimates for the years 2000 and 2024, and the aggregates were calculated as above.

* All references to Kosovo in this report should be understood to be in the context of United Nations Security Council resolution 1244 (1999).

## Representativeness of analysis

Table 3 shows the representativeness of this analysis in terms of under-five and neonatal mortality burden and live births for each equity dimension.

For instance, for the analysis of the under-five mortality rate by wealth quintile, the countries with estimates accounted for `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_wealth_u5$u5_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0435")` per cent of the global under-five deaths and `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_wealth_u5$birth_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "data_livebirths.csv"), "code-number-0436")` per cent of live births in 2024, with approximately `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_wealth_u5$u5_deaths / 1e6, digits = 1, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0437")` million under-five deaths occurring in these countries. For analysis of the neonatal mortality rate by wealth quintile, the countries with survey data accounted for `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_wealth_nmr$nmr_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0438")` per cent of the neonatal deaths and `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_wealth_nmr$birth_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "data_livebirths.csv"), "code-number-0439")` per cent of the live births. For the rural versus urban country-level analysis, the countries accounted for `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_residence_country$u5_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0440")` per cent of the global under-five deaths, `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_residence_country$nmr_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0441")` per cent of neonatal deaths and `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_residence_country$birth_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "data_livebirths.csv"), "code-number-0442")` per cent of live births in 2024, translating into `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_residence_country$u5_deaths / 1e6, digits = 1, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0443")` million under-five deaths. For the rural/urban aggregates, the countries accounted for `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_residence$u5_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0444")` per cent of the global under-five deaths, `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_residence$nmr_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0445")` per cent of neonatal deaths and `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_residence$birth_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "data_livebirths.csv"), "code-number-0446")` per cent of live births in 2024, with about `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_residence$u5_deaths / 1e6, digits = 1, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0447")` million under-five deaths. China and India could not be included in the aggregates since the distribution of births by residency was not available from the sample vital registration data. The subnational estimates by UN IGME (‘Subnational 1’) refer to LMICs with survey data.<sup>72</sup> The countries with estimates accounted for `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_subnational_lmic$u5_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0448")` per cent of global under-five deaths (around `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_subnational_lmic$u5_deaths / 1e6, digits = 1, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0449")` million under-five deaths in total), `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_subnational_lmic$nmr_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0450")` per cent of neonatal deaths and `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_subnational_lmic$birth_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "data_livebirths.csv"), "code-number-0451")` per cent of live births in 2024. ‘Subnational 2’ – which includes `r note_number(coverage_subnational_umhic$countries, "29", "country-p76-subnational", "subnational vital-registration country records; subnational_umhic_codes")` upper-middle- and high-income countries – accounted for only `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_subnational_umhic$u5_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0452")` per cent of global under-five deaths, `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_subnational_umhic$nmr_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0453")` per cent of neonatal deaths and `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_subnational_umhic$birth_percent, digits = 0, evidence = "data_livebirths.csv"), "code-number-0454")` per cent of live births in 2024, with a total of `r code_number_display(calc_black(coverage_subnational_umhic$u5_deaths, digits = 0, evidence = "UNIGME2025_Country_Rates_&_Deaths.csv"), "code-number-0455")` under-five deaths in these countries.

## About us

UNICEF, the United Nations agency for children, works to protect the rights of every child, everywhere – especially the most disadvantaged children in the toughest places to reach. Across more than 190 countries and territories, we do whatever it takes to help children survive, thrive and fulfil their potential.

UNICEF Office of Strategy and Evidence – Innocenti accelerates progress for children by working to ensure that policies and programming are informed by high-quality evidence. As the global custodian of child-related official statistics, it works closely with governments and partners to strengthen national statistical systems. Through world-leading data, research and foresight, it underpins UNICEF’s global leadership on children’s rights and serves as the organization's hub for setting strategy and monitoring programmes. With the active engagement of young people and other partners, it supports advocacy and dialogue aimed at improving the lives of children everywhere.

### Published by

UNICEF Office of Strategy and Evidence – Innocenti Via degli Alfani, 58 50121, Florence, Italy

Email: innocenti@unicef.org Web: unicef.org/innocenti | data.unicef.org Social media: @UNICEFInnocenti on Bluesky, Instagram, LinkedIn, and YouTube

write.csv(note_audit_results, file.path(note_audit_directory, "results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
country_count_audit_directory <- file.path(project_root, "output/qa/country-count-calculated-2026-09-17")

write.csv(country_snapshot_counts, file.path(country_count_audit_directory, "summary-fractions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(subset(note_audit_results, grepl("^country-", occurrence_id) |
  occurrence_id %in% c("code-number-0274", "code-number-0312")),
  file.path(country_count_audit_directory, "results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
country_count_sets <- list(residence_extra = residence_extra_codes,
  birthinterval_map = birthinterval_map_codes,
  birthinterval_aggregate = note_country_sets$birthinterval$U5MR,
  birthinterval_trend = trend_country_codes(trend_country_projection, "birthinterval"),
  birthorder_trend = trend_country_codes(trend_country_projection, "birthorder"))
write.csv(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(country_count_sets), function(name) {
  data.frame(selection = name, Country.Code = sort(country_count_sets[[name]]))
})), file.path(country_count_audit_directory, "country-membership.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(dimension = names(trend_retention_percent), percent = trend_retention_percent),
  file.path(country_count_audit_directory, "trend-retention.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(data.frame(source = names(country_count_source_paths), path = country_count_source_paths,
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(country_count_source_paths))),
  file.path(country_count_audit_directory, "sources.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

note_birth_size_contributors <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(note_birth_size_sets), function(indicator) {

}))

ethnicity_audit$Country[ethnicity_audit$ISO3Code == "RKS"] <- "Kosovo (UNSCR 1244)"
write.csv(ethnicity_audit, file.path(ethnicity_audit_directory, "country-comparisons.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
